title: Checkout slows to a halt
summary: Checkout latency climbs until requests time out, and the database is close to its connection limit. Find the cause before the obvious fix breaks something else.
learningObjectives: Relate application worker and pool settings to the database connection limit.
Distinguish a capacity symptom from the slow query that causes it.
Predict how adding workers affects other clients of a shared database.

provenance.notes: Draft written to prove the environment contract. The pool exhaustion pattern is common, but this version is not adapted from a specific incident report.

journeys.label: Browse order history and check out

alert.title: Checkout latency p95 above 2 seconds
alert.summary: Checkout latency has risen steadily and some requests time out. Database connections are near their configured limit.

healthProbes.publicLabel: Background job worker lost its database connection

plantedFault.summary: orders.customer_id has no index, so the order history query scans the table. Four Gunicorn workers with SQLAlchemy pool_size 10 and max_overflow 10 can open 80 connections, and the job worker uses 10 more, against PostgreSQL max_connections 100.

referenceFix.description: Create the missing index without blocking writes, then watch latency and connection use fall.
commands: psql -U postgres -d shop -c 'CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS orders_customer_id_idx ON orders (customer_id);'

traps.description: Raising the Gunicorn worker count multiplies pooled connections past max_connections, so the job worker sharing the database can no longer connect.

hints.text: Check how many database connections are open and what they are waiting on, for example in pg_stat_activity.
Look at the query plan for the slowest request path before changing capacity.

debrief.rootCause: A missing index on orders.customer_id makes the order history query scan the table. Slow queries hold pooled connections longer, and workers multiplied by pool size already approach PostgreSQL max_connections, so requests time out waiting for a connection.
causalChain: The order history query has no usable index and scans the orders table.
Each slow query holds a pooled connection for longer.
The application pools approach max_connections and requests wait for a free connection until they time out.
Adding workers raises connection demand past the limit and starves the job worker that shares the database.

keyEvidence.description: pg_stat_activity shows connections close to max_connections, many active on the order history query.
The query plan for the order history query shows a sequential scan on orders.
The application log shows SQLAlchemy QueuePool timeouts.
Worker and pool settings show the connection budget: 4 workers with pool_size 10 and max_overflow 10.

recommendedRecovery: Inspect pg_stat_activity to see connection use and the queries holding connections.
Run EXPLAIN on the order history query and identify the sequential scan.
Create the index with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY so writes continue.
Keep workers multiplied by pool size within the database connection budget.
